correctness.rationale: Each binary term is an integral affine map with coefficient sum one. The difference map image is gA by Bezout for g the gcd of integer coefficients, including zero, so equality probability is |A[g]|/|A|. Two-variable term coefficients close under 2b-a and generate all integers from 0,1; t_{d+1}=x has probability |A[d]|/|A|. Prime-power numerators of this set recover torsion-subgroup cardinalities and hence all elementary-divisor multiplicities by discrete second differences. A standalone integer verifier exhaustively checked all binary term pairs on 15 finite abelian groups; finite checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: The exact full probability spectrum of each finite Takasaki quandle is a natural 2026-motivated invariant. Unusually, this coarse numerical set recovers all elementary divisors and fully distinguishes finite abelian underlying groups. The theorem gives a meaningful complete infinite-family classification and an if-and-only-if minimality criterion including non-Latin cases, not an arbitrary finite cutoff or table.
